decisions.reason: A cheap accessory with little sunk investment and low visibility has little commitment behind it, but it costs almost nothing to carry in the spare-parts range, so it is likely kept even if sales are modest.

The multi-model box trailer line was featured on the home page and is central to the core trailer business, so the substantial sunk investment and public commitment favour keeping it, with weak pandemic-era results seen as temporary.
Heavy tooling and development investment in the car transporter line, plus its role in reaching professional users and foreign markets, give management strong reasons to justify and continue it.
The low-bed series is a showcased core product line with substantial sunk costs, so persistence is the most likely course.

The high-cover series builds on existing trailer platforms and was publicly promoted, so dropping it would undercut earlier public decisions, while supply disruptions offer a temporary explanation for any weakness.
Its overlap with line B makes it the most likely candidate for consolidation, but its prominent launch and sunk costs suggest gradual merging rather than outright withdrawal within the year.
